note: Ceiling for internal/controlplane, in hand-written non-test Go lines. Build-ignored tools and generated DO-NOT-EDIT output are reported but not counted; see scripts/report-migration-progress.mjs. The bounded-context migration may only move this down. Raising it requires saying why in the same commit.
reason: Raised by 33 for scan-before-install freshness (#16). The policy field (ArtifactSecurityPolicy.MaximumScanAgeSeconds) went to internal/environments/domain and is not counted here; what lands in controlplane is the enforcement, which is inherently this context's: enrichRequiredArtifactAssessments orchestrates the ArtifactScanner port over a whole DesiredState, and freshness is enforced there -- at proposal, where a clock exists -- rather than in the clock-free desired-state Validate, whose purity keeps a generation immutable. The change is a staleness predicate (artifactAssessmentStale), its use to widen the existing rescan trigger from missing-only to missing-or-stale, one negative-value validation, and a threaded clock through three call sites. It cannot move to a bounded context without exporting the scanner port and DesiredState composition to a package built to depend on neither. Grounding note: the issue's premise -- that installs are not gated on scanning -- was false; ArtifactSecurityPolicy already blocked absent and non-PASS scans (with digest coverage) at every plan-producing path and even auto-scanned missing evidence, so only freshness was genuinely missing. The previous 24436 was recorded on 2026-08-15 for the Apollo GraphQL mount.
supersededReason: Raised by 84 for the Apollo GraphQL mount. This is the first rise since the bounded-context migration, and it is wiring rather than behaviour: apollo_graphql.go builds the resolver, binds one request's sources from the authenticated principal, and registers two routes. It cannot live in internal/apollographql because it needs Repository, GovernanceService, HandlerOptions and requireOperatorPrincipal, all of which are this context's -- moving it would mean exporting the monolith's internals to a package that exists to depend on none of them. Fourteen of the 84 lines are newOverviewSource, extracted so the GraphQL interface and the console's overview build one reader's snapshot through one constructor; two constructions could authorize differently, which is exactly the drift Reporting's port comment warns against. Everything the interface actually decides -- the served contract, its provenance, what may be answered and what must be refused -- is 1,200 lines in internal/apollographql and none of it is here. The previous 24352 was recorded on 2026-08-15 for the Execution slice, on the same counting basis.
